utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, everybody. For the record, everyone is here today with the exception of Mr. Nikolic for the Beara Defence team. Accused are all present. General, good morning to you. We are going to proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have Exhibit 5D1225. This is an order from the Drina Corps dated 24th of November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, this is an order for the conduct of activities and ambushes. Could you tell us what in the military terminology "ambushes" mean?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the definition, it belongs to active combat activities, and it's carried out in the following way: The units conceal themselves and sneak up, they wait for the enemy, and this part is defensive, and then at an appropriate moment they respond very quickly, and at that point, this becomes an offensive combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please now look at point 3 of this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, this is on page 2 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: According to this item number 3, the ambushes plan was to be forwarded to the corps command for certification purposes. And just before that, you see that it was the military brigade, which was to draw up the plan as well as the Skelani Battalion. Could you explain what certification mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this order, it is easy to conclude that this is a zone of activity which was kept under control with patrols and ambushes. It was very vulnerable, columns passed through, and the order has been issued for two units to elaborate a plan of ambush activities. As two units were involved in doing this, it's quite normal that the superior command should review their plans and, if necessary, coordinate and harmonise them. And if it had anything to add as regards the time, place, forces, and means, it could do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to now show you 5D1041. Now, this is a warning from the Drina Corps which is sent to the military brigade dated 3rd of December, 1994. This warning refers to the order that we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In light of this warning, can you say on the basis of the text in this document, did the Milici [Realtime transcript read in error, "military"] Brigade carry out the tasks which were entrusted to it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this document sent by the command of the Drina Corps, it is evident that the Milici [Realtime transcript read in error, "military"] Brigade did draw up a plan, but it can also be seen that it did not comply with the plan. They listed some reasons as to why they didn't do so. The command, however, is insisting that they carry out the plan, and the three reasons adduced for non-compliance were not adopted. One can see here that in military terms the task has not been carried out properly, and the command is warning the unit about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau, "military brigade" in line 25 and line 3 should be "Milici Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. Thank you, Your Honour. This is the Milici Brigade. That's how it should be. I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D1042. Now, this is another order from the Drina Corps dated 13th of December, 1994, which is also about ambushes. May we have page 2 of this order, please, both in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you please have a look at the very top of the page, item number 3. And according to this item 3, the organisation and the execution of ambushes activity in the area of responsibility of the Milici Brigade and of the Skelani Battalion between the Zepa and Srebrenica enclaves is to be executed by the Drina Corps command. Is this order related to the order we just saw?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order is connected with the previous two documents we have looked at. In the first order, the order was given that these two units, the Milici Brigade and the Skelani Battalion, should draw up a plan of ambush activities and submit it for approval. One can see that this was done. From the second document, we can see that it was approved but not implemented, and this is the third level. The corps command saw that those two units, in spite of the plan they had drawn up and in spite of the warning they had received, were not carrying it out, and now this is at the highest level. They are organising the carrying out of ambush activities with their units.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness now be shown Exhibit 5D1043. This is a document from the Main Staff dated 23rd of December, 1994, which forwards the agreement on the cease-fire to the subordinated units. Could we please have page 2 of this document, the last paragraph on page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So here we have the cease-fire agreement which is mentioned, and in the last part of this document you can see that the Main Staff is asking its subordinated units and commands to immediately inform all of the subordinated units to the command of the content of the agreement. Is it usual in an army to send such agreement texts up to the lowest levels of command, lowest levels of command?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To understand this decision concerning this agreement, one must understand two points: First, this is the end of 1994 when the international community is investing enormous efforts into brokering a cease-fire, and the former American President Jimmy Carter was involved in this personally. Every successful command of units in any army rests primarily on providing good information. Every member of the army must know what his command is aspiring to and what his state, his country, is aspiring to. This is a document showing how units are kept well-informed and how it is required if one is to command to provide good information to the units. In this way, every member of the Army of the Republika Srpska would be familiar with the aims and scope of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would now like to show you another agreement which dates from 23rd of -- I mean, this one was from 23rd of December. The one I want to show now is dated 31st of December. This is 5D1045. The date of the agreement is 31st of December. This is the Drina Corps command which delivers the full text of the agreement on the full cessation of hostilities, and this document of the Drina Corps is dated 2nd of January, 1995. Could you please first look at page 2 of this text, item 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to come back to B/C/S in page 1. In English, it will still be page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please read item number 2, which is at the very bottom of the B/C/S text, and could you please do it out loud because I am not sure that the translation in English is precise enough.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "As regards the commitments of the VRS from the agreement, issue necessary preparatory orders for the preparation of firing and combat positions for weapons and for the accommodation of men and combat hardware, as well as the preparation of observation posts, the organisation of communications, et cetera."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Does this order refer to the preparation of combat positions and firing positions or the preparation for setting up whatever is necessary for firing purposes?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very clear here. It says that all these positions should be put in order so that people and equipment can be accommodated there, and to put in order observation post. So this means that all this should be put in order.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you please explain what this "put in order of the facilities of combat positions" actually means?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like when you are redecorating your apartment. When a unit is engaged in combat activities, they have major movements, changes of combat positions. Some combat positions are taken up very quickly. In the course of combat, elements of the combat disposition can get mixed up. So now is the time to put in order the place where you are, and this is what we describe as militarising the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now have 5D1356. This is a document from the 8th OG Srebrenica from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina which is sent to the Zepa Brigade on the 18th of February, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In what way is the first paragraph of this document part of the agreement on cessation of hostilities that we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an example which is directly opposite to what we saw in the previous document. The command of the Drina Corps and the units of the VRS issued orders to put in order firing positions, accommodation for men and equipment, and to put in order all the elements that were missing. Here, the units are being raised to the highest level of combat readiness. This implies that at the simplest and quickest command, the unit can be ready to enter into combat. So the unit must be ready to enter into combat at any moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you document 5D1130, 3-0. This is the report from the Main Staff which is sent to the president of the republic and to the corps on 25th of February, 1995. And I would like to have page 3 on the screen, please, both in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This document gives some information on the situation in the Drina Corps. Now, what I am interested in is to know on the basis of which elements does a superior command - and in this case, the Main Staff - which described in its reports the situation in the subordinated units?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see that this document contains two points for every unit. First, A, enemy; and secondly, B or -- well, it's not quite legible, the situation in the corps, the command and units. So the superior command is collecting information about the situation in the enemy ranks and in the ranks of the unit. It summarises these data and forwards them to the Commander-in-Chief and all units at that level. So the Main Staff of Republika Srpska is drawing up this document based on reports received from subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D1054, which is the report from the Drina Corps on that same date, 27th of February, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This report from the staff, which we've just seen, does it reflect what is written in this report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we analyse this report of the corps command, we can state that it fully reflects this report. This report is somewhat more detailed; whereas, the report of the corps command is somewhat more general, and that's the normal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this order -- in this report, sorry, of the Drina Corps, one may see that certain actions are mentioned which have been executed from the enclave of Srebrenica, and this is the 27th February, 1995, is the date of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1055. That is an order from the Main Staff of -- dated 28th February, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Please have a look at this order and tell us whether it's possible to establish a link between the report of the Drina Corps of the 27th of February and this order of the 28th February, 1995.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is fully in compliance with the former reports and with the situation in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What is the nature of this order? Is it an offensive order, an order for an offensive?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We can see from this report, too, that the Army of Republika Srpska was determined to comply with the cease-fire and that it ordered all its units defensive activities. However, in spite of all this, it is closely monitoring the activities in the battle-field, but that is of less importance. What is important is that it is under attack from the enclave, and in order to prevent those attacks it is now just raising the level or the readiness of the units in order to be able to reply or to react to the attacks in order for the units to be ready to be engaged if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1057. This is an order of the Drina Corps dated 1st March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This order follows an order of the Main Staff of the 28th February - you can see the reference which is made to it in this order - but I'd like to know if this order is essentially different from the order we saw yesterday and which was dated 1994 concerning the separation of the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order is in keeping with everything that they have undertaken so far; in other words, they -- it does not differ. This is an order where they are trying to resolve a problem that they have had since 1993, the problem being the separation of these two enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We mentioned several times the Spreca operation, which was planned on the basis of Directive number 7, and I would like you to look at 5D980. This document is linked to the Spreca operation. 5D980. This document comes from the Drina Corps. Its addressed -- sent to the Main Staff, to the Chief of the Staff. When a document is addressed like that to the Chief of Staff of the Main Staff, who is the person to whom this order is directed? Who might be this person?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no dilemma about that. This was sent personally to Major General Milenko Zivanovic [as interpreted]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This document starts by: "General, sir ..." I would ask you if you can repeat the name of the general to whom the document is sent because there is a mistake in the transcript, line 22.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was sent personally to the Chief of Staff, General Milovanovic, Manojlo.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This document starts by: "Sir, General ..." Do you have anything to say about the way the document begins? Does it mean anything specific?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document that was sent to this person and which was among others filed in the log-book where all other combat documents are filed, we can see from this document -- or in this document some things that are not quite common. For instance, the commander of this unit speaks of the successes of his unit. And, in keeping with that, proposes that units that are assigned to the same task and under the command of another corps, that they should take advantage of the attack of our forces and move along their axis. It is also calling for logistical support. Why is this document somewhat unusual? Because it is known that the command that is responsible for this operation, Spreca 95, is precisely the command that this document deals with, which is the East Bosnia Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D981. It is also connected to the Spreca operation. This document is dated 27 April 1995, and it's sent by Drina Corps to General Milovanovic. Could the witness be shown page 2 of the document. In English, it's the third paragraph. In B/C/S, it's the first paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this document, the Drina Corps requests from the Main Staff the designation of an officer who will be charge of coordination of the forces engaged. If the staff after this request determines or designates an officer in charge of coordination, where should he be to be able to perform this coordination, this officer?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first thing that we can conclude from this document is that the entire operation is under the firm command of the Chief of Staff. We can also see that the command of the Drina Corps also communicates with the corps commander personally and asks for some changes in the coordination. And if this request of the Drina Corps was to be satisfied, the officer who was appointed to coordinate the activities would be at the IBK command post or at the forward command post; in other words, at the command post of the corps which is in charge of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Would an officer at Crna Rijeka at the main command post of the Main Staff, could such an officer coordinate those activities?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not even in theory could such a person coordinate those activities because in order to be able to coordinate such activities, that person would need to be fully aware of all the details of the activities, to be fully advised of the orders and corrections to the orders of the commander of the operation, and to be fully aware of the ongoing situation in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1059. This is a document from the Drina Corps of the 20th March, 1995, sent to the commander of the UNPROFOR in the enclave Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You can see in this document that the Drina Corps has problems with the Muslim formations coming out of the enclave. Could you explain the fact that the commander of the Drina Corps has decided to write or send a message to Srebrenica of the commander of UNPROFOR and didn't take any other action, more violent action? How can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is precisely an example of behaviour or conduct that was -- that was normal or common at the time of this agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: General, the interpreters had problems following you. If you could repeat your answer, please, from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I speak even more slowly? All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think that was the problem. You know, it's something about interpretation. It could be something different, catching up. You know, it could be speed, but I don't think it is speed. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I understood. This document is a pattern of behaviour of the Army of Republika Srpska which was in place after the cease-fire agreement was signed. This pattern of conduct precisely regulates the manner and response in each case where there is a cease-fire violation. It is prohibited that any violation of cease-fire should be responded to with any kind of force. In this particular instance, the commander of the Drina Corps in keeping with all the orders of the command of the Republika Srpska Army, in addition to registering this and taking action to oppose this attack and the cease-fire violation, he also warns the person who was supposed to monitor the cease-fire and also the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1349. This is a document from the commander of the DutchBat sent to the president -- sent to -- from Srebrenica on 3rd of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This document mentions a fire which took place just on the border of the enclave. Owing to the fact that the area had to be demilitarised, does this letter of the DutchBat commander seem appropriate to you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This letter, in each of its segments, is inappropriate. For one, on April 3rd the commander of the DutchBat was very well aware that the 8th Combat Group was reconfigured as a division, and he knows the reasons for that as well. Second, the commander of the DutchBat knows that units of the 28th Division would venture out of the enclave to take action. And from this letter, it would appear that he's not concerned by this fact that these units would leave the enclave and engage the -- in action and kill people, but he's concerned if some rounds were fired within the enclave. Among others things, I would say that this is a formal way of taking action, just a formality, a formal action, but not really addressing the essence of the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1329. This is an order from the president of the republic of the 29th of March, 1995, sent to the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska and to the Ministry of the Interior -- the Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this order, one can read that according to the information given by intelligence, 1.500 troops of the Srebrenica Brigade were to be transferred from Srebrenica to Kladanj. If this information is accurate, what were the military reasons to justify this transfer?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be well known that at this point the 25th Division of the land forces, and previously the 8th operations group that was reconstructed as a division, took action, and this was a huge force that was not in use, which was a loss for the army of the -- of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was clear -- and we saw that the spring offensive for everyone was an occasion to take up as much territory as possible, and it was clear that the BH Army would do anything it can to pull out this unit from Srebrenica or to put this unit in action so that it could link up with other units and create its own territory. The information that was obtained after the restructuring was in place and after increased activities of both these units, it was very likely that they would try to pull out this unit, in this particular case, one whole brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1064. This is information gathered from intelligence of the Drina Corps on the 11th of April, 1995. What I am interested in is the last paragraph in English, page 1, and the one-but-last paragraph in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this information, one can read in this paragraph: "[In English] The prevailing mood among inhabitants of Srebrenica is still that they will leave the enclave if a safe corridor is established by the VRS." The prevailing mood among inhabitants. [Interpretation] This information, does it have a military importance? Why is this information given in this report from the intelligence service?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When intelligence officers assess and analyse the enemy, the other side, in addition to assessing them they also have to assess all other circumstances that may have an effect on combat operations. Here, we can see that there is a strong pressure and that the inhabitants of Srebrenica felt that they were used as -- as a human shield by their own forces, and they wished to leave Srebrenica at any possible moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show you now 5D1262. This is a document from the minister of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Hasan Muratovic, and sent to the presidency -- the War Presidency of Zepa on the 8th of May, 1995. This document speaks about the evacuation in the general interest.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you have a look at this document, and could you explain what is meant by the "evacuation in General interest" in this context. In particular, explain the title of this document.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The subject, "Public Evacuation," that is what the subject is, and the rest of the text really discusses evacuation. Simply, we can see that there are two contradictions here: The population has a desire to leave the area under any circumstances, whereas the state and the army want to leave them there. So any conclusions here -- drawing any conclusions would be unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1364. This document comes from the 28th Division, and it's sent to the commander of the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 19th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the first part of this document, which speaks in particular of the problem of departures of members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the civilians' departure from the enclaves. Could you tell us, what were the military reasons or the possible reasons for the authorities of Srebrenica to prevent members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to leave the enclave?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two problems are evident here: The first is desertion; that is, members of the army of Republic leaving, and the second problem is the evacuation of civilians. One can see here what we talked about from the beginning. They all want to leave the area in the direction of Tuzla, Kladanj, and Serbia, so in all three directions. Everywhere -- people feel much safer anywhere else than they do in that area, and it's quite clear to everyone that this is a consequence of the creation of a so-called protected area which was in fact militarised.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What were the reasons for the authorities to prevent members of the army to leave the enclave, which, anyway, had to be demilitarised?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two levels of authority here. The local authorities, wherever they could, expressed the wish to leave the area because they -- they and the population felt insecure; and the state authorities, which wanted both the army and the population to remain in Srebrenica because they knew that in this way they were tying down a large military force. On the other hand, all the members of the army who wanted to leave realised that they would become a legitimate target if they continued to behave as they were behaving, and so they realised that it was best for them to leave. The population, they used as protection and as a source of logistical support, and the civilian authorities wanted to retain their territory in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1065.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is another information coming from the intelligence of the Drina Corps on the 13th of April, 1995. Please look at page 2, last paragraph of the document, which speaks about an offensive, a possible offensive. The connection which this paragraph speaks about, is it a connection with forces coming from the direction of Kladanj, has to do with the forces of Srebrenica? Did they represent a real danger for the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this relatively small zone, the 28th Division being there was a threat to the VRS and the Drina Corps. A special threat was the fact that it was expected that this unit would try to break through the encirclement. They were not in a position to engage in a frontal battle. It was estimated that the greatest threat was at the point where the other units of the BH Army were closest, and in this particular instance this would be Kladanj. This is a realistic assessment of a situation which could arise for the 28th Division to break out of the encirclement, and, on the other side, for the units of the BH Army to take action to reduce the thickness of the separation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1067. This is a document from the Drina Corps of the 25th of April, 1995. Reading this first paragraph, we see that the Drina Corps has received from security services of the Ministry of the Interior some information according to which the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was preparing a general offensive on the positions of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What was -- what is the natural reaction of an army when it receives this sort of information?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When such information is received under normal conditions, any army would take offensive action to prevent the carrying out of this offensive, which was expected from the beginning of the year and was called the Spring Offensive. Bearing in mind that the cease-fire was still in force, the VRS and the Drina Corps did not take offensive action to prevent this offensive in its beginning, in the initial grouping of forces. All they did was to strengthen the organising of continuous reconnaissance, observation, and following of all activities in order to prevent any surprise.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1237. This is an order from the Drina Corps of the 18th of May, 1995, concerning the sealing up of the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa -- sealing off. What I am interested in in this order is the first part of the order itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Essentially, is this order different from preceding orders which had the same goal, which you have already seen?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The introductory part of this order can also be based on the order of 1993 or of 1994 because these are the same tasks of the Drina Corps stemming from its obligation, which it received in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1238. This is a document from the Drina Corps sent to the Main Staff on the 20th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Have a look at the first paragraph. According to this text, it seems that the commander of the Drina Corps has informed the Chief of Staff of the Main Staff about the combat plan and the fact that the organisation of this plan has already started as much as possible at a meeting which took place at the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska on the 20th of May, 1995. The Chief of Staff -- the Chief of the Main Staff to whom this document refers, could tell us who may be this person, this Chief of Staff? Who is it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is evident in this document that this is the Chief of Staff General Manojlo Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Since the Chief of Staff of the Main Staff was informed about the plan for combats around Srebrenica and Zepa on the 20th of May, 1995, and since he is even told about the beginning of implementation of this plan, what may be concluded about the implication of General Milovanovic in May 1995 in the area of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on all the available documents so far, and especially the collection of documents presented today, it can be unambiguously concluded that the situation in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps and the area of responsibility of the IBK was exceptionally familiar to the Chief of Staff, General Manojlo Milovanovic, and not only was he very familiar with the situation, but he was personally in charge of a large number of operations in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you have a look at paragraph 1 of this document -- item 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, it's on page 2. In this item 1, we see that the Drina Corps requests the resubordination of a unit of the 60th Protection Regiment -- 65th. And could the witness now be shown a document of the staff which follows this request, and this is 5D1214. Essentially, this document speaks of a unit of the 65th Protection Regiment which was already resubordinated to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you explain, what is "resubordination"?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Resubordination is an activity where the commanding officer for a certain period of time, for certain tasks gives a unit of his to another commander to command. The other commander during the time in which that unit is resubordinated to him has the right to command the unit, but he does not have the right to make any changes within the unit itself. After the completion of the task, the unit returns to its original commander and reports to him as to how it has carried out its task.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just to be quite clear, who commands with the unit of the 65th Regiment -- protection regiment when this unit is resubordinated to the Drina Corps? Who commands it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Drina Corps was in command of this resubordinated unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the number of this order, 03/4-973. Can you tell us what this number actually means?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not look at the log-book of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, but I conclude that this number refers to the staff because it's the one occurring most frequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What does this number indicate?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This number indicates that this document was drawn up in the Main Staff of the VRS, that it was entered into the log-book under this number, that it was signed by the officer responsible, and that it fulfills all the conditions for being sent out.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: If one supposes that this number is given by the Administration in Charge of Operational and Educational Matters, does the chief of the Administration of Operational and Educational Matters, does he have to necessarily see all the documents who bear such a number?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not just -- not necessarily, but he needn't see them at all because this is a document signed by his superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown document 5D1079. This is a report, interim report, of the Drina Corps of the 27th of May, 1995, informing - you can see in paragraph 1 that the -- that the Drina Corps informs the Main Staff about the fact that five soldiers of the Milici Brigade have been killed in an ambush.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What is the influence of such events on the making of decisions by the command of a unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is evident from this report that this was an exceptional incident in the unit. It was a consequence of lack of discipline, and the consequences were tragic. Based on this report, one can see that the steps taken by the superior command implied that something like this might happen; that is, in the unit there was a lot of irresponsibility in carrying out tasks. So this tragedy was the lack of -- due to the lack of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown 5D1075. This is a new order from the Drina Corps. It concerns the communication between the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa. It's dated 4 June 1995, and as this is simply an order which is very brief.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I have a simple question. Does this order differ essentially of other orders we have already seen concerning communication between the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't differ at all. This is one of the many different activities to carry out a task received earlier, so this is just an attempt to carry out that order.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown order 5D1245. This is also an order from the Drina Corps dated 19 June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you just have a look at the preamble of this order. According to this order, what were the reasons for this order to be sent? According to what you may read on this order, what are the reasons for giving it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Practically, failure to carry out the order on separating the enclaves, the constant problems that the units of the Drina Corps were experiencing in that area, all this prompted another order to have this regular task carried out. So this is one of countless orders attempting to have this task carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: One may see that this order also refers to a new situation on the front around Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please display 5D1092 for the witness. This is an order from the Drina Corps on the 15th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of this order, you may see that in the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps, the enemy has executed combat operations according to Kladanj, Kalesija, Olovo, and between Srebrenica, Zepa, and around Gorazde. This order you have just seen, does it have any connection with this document, the order you saw just before this document, which was dated 19 June.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to mention a fact here, which is the following: The command of the Drina Corps had a very specific position. It had an outside and inside front line, so to speak; that is, its demarcation line with the 2nd Corps, it held that front where there was contact. And then, on the other side, it held the borders of the enclaves where the enemy was extremely active and never stopped activities. The external line had its oscillations. Sometimes there was more activities, sometimes less. It participated in both defensive and offence actions by the command of the Drina Corps. The internal borders so to speak were constantly active. There was never any decrease in activity or, if there was, this was only so that the concentration of the VRS soldiers would fall. And here, we see that at this point there was intensive activity at both the external and internal borders of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break now of 25 minutes. How much more do you think you have?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I will go until the end of the day. Perhaps I will finish a little before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like to show the bottom of the page in B/C/S and page 2 in English. Page 2 in English, and in B/C/S, it's at the very bottom of page 1. You can see under item 1 in this order that this order was given so that all subordinated units to the Drina Corps ensure full combat readiness.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And before asking you the question, I'd like to show you Exhibit 5D1088, which is an interim report from the Drina Corps dated 14th of July [as interpreted], 1995, so the eve of the order that we were looking at.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a small correction. Line 18, page 24, this is the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please consider this interim report and tell us whether there was a connection with the order of full readiness to combat and the situation described in this report.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous order on raising combat readiness to the maximum was precisely the consequence of these activities that had been undertaken by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D1249, which is an order from the Drina Corps from 27th of June, 1995. 1249 is the number of the exhibit. Now, this is another order about the situation around the Zepa and Srebrenica enclaves. Now, we looked at a number of reports dating from June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Why was it necessary to issue this new order on the 27th of June, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At every point where there is a new situation or new combat activity one cannot follow the orders that had been issued earlier, it is necessary to issue new orders and correct the previous orders. We could say here that the entire collection of these orders by the Drina Corps, on the basis of BH Army actions in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps and a newly developed situation, this is a natural live organism of commanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D1246. This is an order from the Drina Corps dated 19th of June, 1995. Could we please have page 2 in English. For B/C/S, it will be page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You can see in this order that the Main Staff ordered the Krajina and Drina Corps to form a light infantry brigade, each of them, so as to reinforce the Sarajevo Corps. And this, indeed, is the order of the Drina Corps to set up this brigade. How do you explain that in a situation in which the Drina Corps possibly had problems in its own area, that they had to send a brigade to the Sarajevo Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably because the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska assessed - and based on all the analysis so far I agree with their assessment - that the Drina command Corps could with their forces resolve all their problems, especially the problems surrounding the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa, and it assessed that at this point in time the Sarajevo Romanija Corps had bigger problems and, pursuant to that, decided to assign a unit for the implementation of the task that they had to implement. This was the method where from the complement of the existing live units you would withdraw one unit and form it to assign it to a particular task, and this is a well-known method of work. The order is in every way justified, and it has its purpose, and it would in no way interfere with the structure of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have Exhibit P107. This is the order from the Drina Corps about combat -- active combat activities from the 2nd of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you please say what active combat activities are? Can you define them, please?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to be as precise and as clear as possible. Active combat activities are primarily offensive activities that are carried out by the army, and among them we know counter-attack in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the witness please slowly repeat the types of counter-attack and response in combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: General, again, we have a few problems. If you could kindly repeat the types of counter-attack and response in combat because the interpreters had some problems.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I will repeat it. Active combat activities are primarily offensive activities; mainly, they involve attacks. Among them we know the following: counter-attack, insurgence, entrapment, diversion, demonstrative operations. Based on the forces that conduct these attacks, they are carried out by tactical units. The fact that they are carried out by tactical units speak of their scope and the number of people that participate in them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I just briefly show you now Exhibit P114. This is the order from the Drina Corps dated 13th of July, 1995. This is the order for the attack to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Why in this order it is -- the attack is mentioned, while the other order mentioning the Srebrenica enclave, it mentioned combat activities?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is precisely the substantial difference between these two orders that have been issued. The attack order, in such an order an attack is a form of combat operations, and this is what would determine the final goal and the forces that would take part in it with a clear -- clearly defined beginning and end of an operation. Active combat operations in their character are subordinated to the attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the very last part of your answer about the comparison between combat activities and the attack, please.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I should interpret because I think that the term "suposirenja" [phoen] was not properly interpreted. An active attack has its continuity, whereas the act of operations can fluctuate. They are not in continuation. They can be conducted, and then there can be a pause in their carrying out, and then they can be on again.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, before talking in greater detail about activities taking place around Srebrenica in July 1995, I would like to show you Exhibit P2894, which is an order from the Drina Corps dated 2nd of June, 1995, and which is about Zeleni Jadar, the communication in Zeleni Jadar. Could you please look at the first page of this order, and I think that this should suffice for you to be able to express your opinion. And could you please say whether this order is connected to the activities which then took place in July? Can this action be considered as the beginning of the action which was initiated in July?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This action is one of a number of actions and problems that they had in this area, and it is not a beginning of anything. It is just in continuation of the attempt to resolve a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You can see here that this order is about the establishment of physical control over the buildings and communications in Zeleni Jadar. I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D1227, which is an order from the Drina Corps from 18th of March, 1995. Now, this is what I am interested in. This is about property in Zeleni Jadar. The purpose of this order, is it connected to the order we just saw, the order from 2nd of June, 1995? Is there a connection between the purposes or the goals of these two orders?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In both of these documents, the subject is Zeleni Jadar, and we can see that this is an area that is outside of the demilitarised zone, and we can see that the Army of Republika Srpska is seeking to establish control in keeping with all the authority in its power.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now come back to Exhibit P107, i.e., the order from the Drina Corps from 2nd of July, 1995. Could we have page 3 in English and 2 in B/C/S, please, and I'd like to focus on item number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Looking at the content of the task indicated in item 2, does this in essence defer to the tasks that were given to the Drina Corps previously? Does it differ? Is it different from the tasks which were previously entrusted to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since 1993, the Drina Corps' task was to ensure the security of the enclaves, of the enclave borders, so that they may function in agreement -- or according to the agreement that had been reached. And the minute that those borders became porous, especially between the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves, their duty was to split them apart and establish control in the area again. So that was their task since 1993, and there was really nothing new in this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: From a military point of view, does point 2 in this order imply that the civilian population be displaced?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In no way can that be the conclusion, and it is even very difficult to draw such a conclusion even if we were to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What about the task defined in this order? Does it imply that the enclaves be eliminated?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to read it in its entirety, and then I would say that the last sentence is very precise: Within the depth of the area, to split apart the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica, and reduce them to their urban areas. So the term used here is "split apart," not "taking over."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, what about the Administration in Charge of Operations and Training in the Main Staff? Did it have a role in the planning of this it order?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Administration For Operations and Training had no role or authority or any part in the creation and issuance of this order nor any orders that we spoke of today.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit P33, which is a document from the Main Staff dated 9th of July, 1995, which delivers to the Drina Corps the agreement -- agreement of the president of the Republika Srpska for the forces of the Army of Republika Srpska to enter Srebrenica and, also, the order of the president concerning the procedure to be applied with the members of UNPROFOR and the Muslim civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: First of all, can you say how important this document is, from 9th of July, 1995, as part of the events which unfolded in July 1995 in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please scroll this down a bit?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please scroll down the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Looking at the substance of the document, first I would like to say that this does not come from the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska Army. This was a document that was only filed there. This is a decision by the supreme commander, which was forwarded to the subordinates by the assistant commander, and it was received and filed in the Main Staff. So in its character and by its nature, this is not a decision from the Main Staff. It is a decision by the supreme commander. And according to this document, this decision of the supreme commander refers to taking up -- or taking over Srebrenica and demilitarising the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Who or what organ in the Main Staff is normally in charge of forwarding the orders to the subordinated authorities?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, it was irrelevant. What was relevant was that the authorised organ of the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska Army, the assistant commander, was aware of the decision of the supreme commander; and being briefed of it, he relayed it to all the other sides or to all the other bodies, and where it was actually filed is not relevant for this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with respect to the answer that the witness gave, it is non-responsive to the question, and I would ask if he could actually answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Unless you wish to disagree, but I think Mr. Vanderpuye is perfectly right in pointing that out. The question, General, was as follows: "Who or what organ in the Main Staff, is under normal circumstances normally in charge of forwarding the orders to the subordinate authorities?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that I may complicate matters when I answer, but each organ within his sphere or his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall make my question more precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Go ahead, but you still need to clarify this because the question was either "who" as a person or, if there is an organ that is charged with passing on instructions, which organ would that be. So if you could perhaps -- if you need to consult with your client, by all means. Okay, let's proceed then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'd like you to tell me, what is the organ, theoretically, in the Main Staff which conveys the orders about combat activities to the subordinated units?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a matter of principle, combat documents, or the basic combat documents, are issued from the staff or from the operations and training organ from the operations centre. But all the other documents would go -- or be issued by their organs. So this is what I can say to make it more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So why -- or do you know, what are the possible reasons why this specific document did not or was -- did not arise or was not recorded or signed by an officer from the Administration for Operations and Training in the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is evident from this document that the president of Republika Srpska had been informed of the results, that General Tolimir was there, that somebody conveyed to them the results, and at that point the supreme commander ordered the assistant commander to convey his standpoint. The assistant commander at that point in time conveyed the standpoint from the most convenient place available to him. So this document need not have been logged with the operations and training organ or the staff or anywhere else. It was entered into the log in the nearest place where the assistant commander could go to have it forwarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is there anything in this document which may indicate that the Administration for Operations and Training has received this document, that it has finally arrived there to the Administration for Operations and Training?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the content of the document and all the activities, it was not sent there, and it was sent to Generals Gvero and Krstic at the forward command post and the command of the Drina Corps and also for information to the president of the republic. So it's clear from this to whom it was sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What was the role of the Administration for Operations and Training in the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and of General Miletic who was heading it in the conduct of combat activities in Srebrenica in July 1995? I am asking you this question on the basis of the documents which you have been able to peruse and about the usual role of the administration of the staff under such circumstances.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this entire collection of documents presented here, the role of the Administration for Operations and Training was merely on the basis of the combat reports coming from the Drina Corps to -- to take note of these reports, incorporate them into the reports to the Main Staff, and forward them. When some reports arrive which are of a special nature, something that is unusual, then the Administration for Operations and Training or another administration which is competent for this aspect has to warn the commander of this. This does not refer to units where the commander is already there because then the administration would know that the commander was already familiar with the situation in the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And just to clarify, in the situation we are interested in, we know that General Mladic is in the area of Srebrenica at least on the 11th and the 12th of July. Now, in this period of time did General Miletic, who is in Crna Rijeka if he was there - let's assume that he's there - was he to make some proposals, warnings, or issue warnings about Srebrenica to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assuming that he was there and the person who was deputising for him was not there, if he learned of this report he would have no competence to deal with it because he would see that this was something not falling within the plans in the Main Staff of Republika Srpska and that it represents activities in the Drina Corps and that the commander is in the area and is aware of all this. And even if the commander was anywhere else, one of his assistants, the one who drew up this report, would be aware of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the normal course of circumstances in the Army of Republika Srpska, did the Administration in Charge of Operations and Training, was it in charge of supervising the moving or the evacuation of the population?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday - and I'll be more precise now - the VRS did not have organs working directly or indirectly with the population. It had no -- or, rather, the operations and training administration had no competency whatsoever to deal with the population, and this is the case in all armies.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it possible to monitor -- generally speaking, is it possible to monitor or supervise the evacuation taking place in Srebrenica, Potocari, if you're in Crna Rijeka, which is several tens of kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such activities which involve a large number of participants and a great frequency of occurrence can only be monitored or controlled on the spot, not at a distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Document P113, which is a report about the evacuation which took place in Srebrenica, dated 13th of July, 1995, and which Colonel Radoslav Jankovic sent to the administration of intelligence of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, we can see on this document that it was sent to the administration of intelligence, intelligence department. What about the officers who worked in operations and evacuations affairs? Should these officers have known about a document which was in fact sent to another department?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think it would be useful if my colleague could repeat the question. It's not translated correctly in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This document comes from the sector in charge of security and intelligence and was sent to the intelligence department in the Drina Corps. Should the officers in charge of the Administration of Operational Affairs and Training in the Main Staff have been made aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In every army, it is the practice - and it was the same in the Main Staff of the VRS - that whenever one organisational unit receives a report or an order, as soon as it looks at it, it should see whether there are any elements contained within it of which another organisational unit should know. If there are such elements present, then it must inform the other organisational unit. This document was sent to the sector for intelligence and security. It contains about five paragraphs. The first three in the nature of things refer mostly to the logistics sector or the sector for the rear, and that sector was then supposed to be informed of this. The fourth one concerning theft refers to the Administration for Security; it's within their competence. And the fifth one would be for the information organs or state organs for information. In other words, there is not a single element of this document referring to the Operations and Training Administration. It doesn't fall within their purview.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And one last question about Srebrenica. I'd like to show you Exhibit 5D1365. This is a document from the presidency of Srebrenica, from the president, which was sent to the president of the republic on the 9th of July, 1995, the president of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, what can you say about the position of the local authorities, the local Srebrenica authorities, about the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at this document, we can see two things: That the civilian authorities do not know what the 28th Division is planning and doing; and secondly, they insisted from day one that a method should be found to evacuate the population from Srebrenica. Their desire to have this done is constant.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to come back to Exhibit P114. This is the order about the attack on the Zepa enclave from 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: First of all, could you tell us, what was the role of the Administration for Operations and Training in the Main Staff? What was supposed to be its role in the issuance of such an order?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the order of the command of the Drina Corps to some of its units and for the carrying out of regular tasks, the Administration for Operations and Training had no role at all in the issuance of this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Should this order have been sent to the Administration of Operations and Training of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, by no means. Orders sent to the Main Staff for its approval are clearly defined what orders they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness be shown page 2 of this order, which is also page 2 in English. Sorry, in B/C/S this is still page 1, and actually, also page 1 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please look at items 2, 3, and 4. Is there anything, which -- of course, from a military standpoint, is there anything in these items which imply activities of displacement of the civilian population or any activities against the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no element leading to such a conclusion. The command of the Drina Corps based on the decision of the Commander-in-Chief with respect to Srebrenica and based on the results achieved in eliminating the Srebrenica enclaves extended activities in the direction of Zepa, and they knew that they were holding stable the line facing the 2nd Corps. So this is exclusively the planning of military action in relation to the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness be shown 5D1366. This is a document from the presidency -- the War Presidency of the Zepa municipality, which was sent to the president of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on 19th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please look at this document, particularly with a focus on items 1 and 2 and the end of this page, which actually is the following page in English, and tell us what conclusion you can draw as to the position of the Zepa authorities about the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document indicates very clearly that there was antagonism between the local authorities and the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. There is a sentence here which is quite clear: I don't know what to say about your plan. This is the plan that they should remain in Zepa. They are insisting on leaving Zepa. In any case, it's better for someone to be saved than for someone to stay. So the local authorities want the people to leave Zepa whereas the state authorities want them to stay, and we can see that this issue has already been discussed, and they expect that it has also been discussed at the Security Council of the UN.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What we have in the transcript is not very clear. Who insists that the population should stay in Zepa, and who insists on the fact that the population should leave Zepa?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The state authorities always insisted that the local population should remain in Zepa, and in this way they could achieve their goals, whereas the local authorities always insisted that they leave Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show you Exhibit 5D1350. This Exhibit is in English, but I'm going to read the relevant part to you. This is a statement from the president of the Security Council dated 20th of July, 1995, about the situation in Zepa, and the paragraph that I am interested in is the one-before-last of this statement, which reads that the Security Council president said the following: [In English] "The Security Council underlines the importance it attaches to the fullest cooperation with UNHCR and other international humanitarian organisations and demands that they be given unhindered freedom of movement and access to the area. It further demands that the Bosnian Serb authorities cooperate with all efforts, including those of UNPROFOR, to ensure the safety of the civilian population, and in particular its most vulnerable members, including evacuation as requested by the Foreign Minister of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in his letter of 17 July 1995." [Interpretation] Now, once you've seen this document, could you say what seems to be the position about all the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina about Zepa?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document provides the reply to the previous document. We can see that whoever submitted the previous document was aware of the fact that the issue had been raised before the Security Council on the 17th of July. He called up on the 19th to see what had been done, that the issue of evacuation would be raised, which was what they wished, and he asked to see what the Security Council would do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, if the authorities of Republika Srpska were aware about this content of the declaration of the president of the Security Council, what could be their conclusions about the willingness of the Muslim people in Zepa about evacuation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The authorities of Republika Srpska were certainly aware of this document, and it was clear to them that it was the will of the population to be evacuated from the enclave, and it's also clear what obligations were imposed upon them by the Security Council in relation to the population and the wounded for their safety.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You can see that in this document the Security Council calls for a cooperation with the international organisations. I would like now to show you document 5D1114. This is a document from the Drina Corps from 20th of July, 1995, giving the information about the authorisation granted by the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska to the Red Cross for the purposes of medical evacuation of the sick and wounded persons in Zepa. As we look this document, can you see something which is an irregularity or a disagreement, something which disagrees with the call made in the statement of the Security Council -- by the Security Council president?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is evident from this document that the Main Staff of the VRS reacted as required by the document of the Security Council, the portion we've read out, and we can see that they carried out their obligations in-depth very fast from the Main Staff toward the corps, and the corps urgently complied with their obligations in relation to the subordinate units. So we can see that this document is in line with the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness now be shown Exhibit 5D1115. This is a similar document from the Drina Corps dated 20th of July, 1995, which is about the authorisation for the members of UNPROFOR -- for a team of UNPROFOR to go to Zepa on 20th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Does this document conform with what has been asked by the Security Council?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a clear example that they were in compliance with the Security Council document and that they promptly moved to regulate this issue from the Main Staff all the way down to the actual people who were to implement it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We know that the evacuation was not done on the 20th of July, 1995, and I would like to show you two documents of the 25th of July, 1995. The first one is 5D1117. This is a document from the Drina Corps giving -- getting authorisation of the main staff to UNPROFOR to command the -- before I ask the question, I would like to show you another document. First, please have a look at this one. I would like you to have a look now to 5D1118. The document is quite similar, on the 25th of July, 1995, giving authorisation for a convoy, a Russian and French convoy, including for the medical transport to go into Zepa on the 25th of July, 1995. What can you tell us about this last document in comparison with the appeal of the president of the Security Council?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this document was produced on the 25th, we can see that there is a continuity in the implementation of the Security Council decisions relating to UNPROFOR, the UNHCR, et cetera, the Red Cross, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last document on this matter, 5D1120, of the 27th of July, 1995, giving authorisation for the movement of a convoy of UNPROFOR transporting food and water to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What is your comment about this document?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, like all the previous ones, are just a continuation of the approval provided by the Main Staff of the corps command to the -- to those individuals who were to implement them to follow and imply with all the orders issued by the Security Council document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown document 5D1381. This is a document on the police station of Rogatica, 27 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I just have a question concerning the reasons why the police station of Rogatica informs the Ministry of the Interior on how the evacuation is taking place.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The normal job of public security was to monitor the situation in the territory, and this is part of their responsibility, to inform the organs on what the situation in the territory is. And in this particular case, we see that they are dealing with an extraordinary event, evacuation, and their reporting was a natural and normal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The fact that this -- the fact that Mr. Markovic informs his superiors of the evacuation, which is ongoing and -- an ongoing operation, mean that in any way that he is himself taking part in this evacuation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this document, I could judge that he knew of the evacuation. Now, who was responsible for implementing or commanding or -- in this operation, it is hard to say, but this gentleman was aware of the operation, he been informed of it, and he was informing that he would follow-up with any changes in the situation in his reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown document 5D1113. This is a document from the deputy commander for logistics of the Main Staff dated 19 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you have a look at items 1 and 2 of this order in which transport means and medical team are mentioned as well as medical equipment and the assistant for logistics gives an order for these transport means and medical means may be allowed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, it is item 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So these tasks which are described here in items 1 and 2, are they within the purview of the logistics sector?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we analyse these two points in detail, points 1 and 2, we can see that point 1 deals practically with the traffic service, that part of it relates to the technical service, and in one part of it we are dealing with supplies, in this case, of fuel, which is the natural purview of the rear sector. The only problem here is the problem of buses because the Republika Srpska Army did not own or have any buses in their hardware, so they must have procured them from somewhere else. As for item 2, it is exclusively in the logistics sector, within the purview of the logistics sector and its chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... look at item 4. In this item, one had to assure that a unit of the police, through the chief of Administration in Charge of Operational and Training, this police unit was necessary about looking after the war booty. Which were the competencies of the chief of the administration in charge of operations and training when he received this document? What was he able to do?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please scroll down this document a bit. Thank you. The Administration for Operations and Training does not have any competence over military police units. We can see that this document this officer sent to the command post, to the basic command post, the competence of this administration or the basic command post was to advise of the contents of this information, the sector of intelligence, which had the military police within its competence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D3015. D3015. P3015. 3015. [In English] No, 3015, sorry. It's my fault. [Interpretation] Excuse me. 3015. No, in English it was my fault.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this, you can see that General Krstic who at the time was the commander of the Drina Corps requests engagement of a military police unit in the enclave of Zepa in order to -- which was necessary for organising and collecting the war booty and prevent any looting. This document is dated 20 July 1995, and the document we just saw before that was the 19th July, 1995. Do you see any connection between the two documents?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see some similarities and some differences. The similarities are in the following: The first document was sent to the forward command post, and this document here was sent to the -- to General Miletic personally and with a request for a military police battalion. But they both deal with one and the same matter. The military police had never been nor could it be within the competence of the Administration for Operations and Training. During combat operations and in many situations, a large number of officers, when they need to resolve an issue, then they try to send something to a person. So if you are to send something to a command post and wish that to be forwarded to another command post, then you would send it personally to the commander, for instance, Commander Miletic [as interpreted], and then he would personally send it or forward it to the Administration of Operations and Training for implementation.
