But there is mention here of a request for a military police unit, but this document will probably in the end reach the right address where it was meant for.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just a correction concerning the transcript, page 45, line 21. What did you say for the first document? Was it sent to the command post, the main command post or the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first document says "command post," "KM." Then -- when it says "KM," then mainly what they mean is the main command post.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Basic. Interpreter's correction: the basic command post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did the witness say Commander Miletic in line 5 of page 46?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't think so, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Have you at any time spoken about Commander Miletic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said KM command post, and at one point I noticed in the transcript that for "KM" there was "Kosovo and Metohija," and then it was deleted.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: There is another mistake in the transcript. Did you say that this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It still doesn't explain who else he mentioned instead of Commander Miletic, because from the transcript itself, to me its obvious that he did mention a name, even though it wasn't Commander Miletic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can repeat what I've said from the start: The only thing that is certain that I never mentioned Commander Miletic because I never saw or mentioned his name in this expert report. The first document that was sent was sent to the KM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I don't think we need to repeat everything. I will just read out to you the relevant part, and then you tell us who did you mention: You said: "So if you are to send something to a command post and wish that it be" -- "wish it to be forwarded to another command post, then you would send it personally to the commander, for instance ..." And then we have "Commander Miletic." Who did you mention: Commander whoever, "... and then he would personally send it or forward it to the Administration for Operations and Training for implementation." In the example that you gave, who did you mention as being the person forwarding the information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Miletic [as interpreted]. I never said "Commander Miletic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There still is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: To whom did General Miletic transmit this information, in particular, the information contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document would have to be forwarded to the sector for security and intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see document P186. This is a document from the Main Staff security and intelligence department dated 29 July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Please look at paragraph 3 of the document and tell us whether this paragraph corresponds to the competencies of the organ in charge of intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to intervene with a small correction. The way it was translated was that this was from the intelligence and security department, but in fact it is from the intelligence and security sector. Secondly, the third paragraph, when we look at the way it has been written but also based on its substance, we can see that it is not something that is within the purview of the intelligence and security sector.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Organ, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you give an explanation, why did General Tolimir have this document done for something which is outside of his own competence?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see that he forwarded this document to General Krstic personally. Probably, and this is just my assessment, in order to be more emphatic, he appeared to issue an order in this sentence. However, from all the other documents that we've seen so far, I don't think that there were any breaches of the chain of command and subordination.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You can see in this paragraph that indeed the Drina Corps was supposed to take all possible measures to prevent the Zepa Brigade to come out of its encircled position. Did it have -- in military terminology, is breaking the encircling have any specific meaning?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "break through from the encirclement" is not a military term. The word -- the military term is "break out on encirclement," so this is rather unusual the way it's been used here.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you conclude from this document what General Tolimir was thinking about when he speaks about breaking through the circle?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my military assessment, this is an instruction, a request, sent to the commander to try and do -- and use everything in his power to prevent the break through from the encirclement but, rather, to try and resolve the problem within the encirclement with his own unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown document --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just before this, from a military point of view this paragraph, this precise paragraph, does it concern the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire paragraph refers exclusively to military personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown P3036. This is a document from the Podrinje Brigade dated 1st August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you have a look at this text in total?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go back at the very beginning of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: At the beginning of the document, we may see that it's about the movement of enemy groups from the Zepa enclave, the group of enemies breaking through the enclave of Zepa. After that, in the first paragraph it speaks of Muslim forces, and after that, in the third paragraph the enemy groups are mentioned. There are directions indicated which these groups are following. And finally, at the end --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you show the bottom of the document in B/C/S, and in English it would be page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Here, at the end we can see the term "sweeping" [as interpreted] and "balai" and essentially Muslims. From a military point of view, does this paragraph have to do anything with the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by this entire document that was produced by this chief of the intelligence organ of this brigade, there is always mention of BH Army members, but they keep using different terms. So sometimes it is difficult to put all this in context. The terms in use are not typically military terms or they are used in error, and it is not clear to me at all why he would send a document like this to anyone other than his immediate superior. So if we were to analyse this document we could conclude that he means members of BH Army throughout the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Before we have the break, I noticed that in your question, Ms. Fauveau, you started by saying: "Here, at the end we can see the term 'sweeping' and then 'balija.'" I am trying to find the words "sweeping." It think it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if you could kindly say which word you had mentioned apart from balija, which word you had referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I didn't say about sweeping. Perhaps I used a derogatory term.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "balai" and not "balija."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That makes it more confusing to me. I think I need 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't think I said anything about sweeping, but maybe I used a derogatory term. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's have -- yes, but I don't see another derogatory term in the -- in the document. Let's have a 25-minute break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to clarify things, when I use the word "balije," I used this word which is used in the document which I quoted from the document in the paragraph-before-last.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Note from the interpreter: The term was confused with "balayer," which means "to sweep" in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that. In fact, I thought about that, and I made two and two together. You should speak your French a little bit more slowly, it means.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we show the top part of this document to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Amongst others, this document is addressed to General Miletic. What were the competencies of the head of Administration for Operations and Training and of the administration in the tracking of enemy groups throughout the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Administration for Operations and Training has nothing to do with intelligence activities. This was sent by the intelligence organs to his services, and by some sort of inertia, it was also sent to the basic command post. Surveillance of enemy forces and the conditions in which they are operating is precisely defined as falling within the competence of the intelligence organs headed by the intelligence administration in the sector for intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What is the role for the Administration for Operations and Training during the surrender of soldiers from the enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with prisoners either, no competencies and no obligations. It doesn't fall within its purview.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D1373. This is a document from the security services, from the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, from the Gorazde sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And I would like you to look at paragraph -- at the last paragraph, which talks about groups of combatants who crossed the border and who entered Yugoslavia. According to this document, which stems from the Muslim authorities, were civilians involved in the crossing of the border, and are they concerned here by this last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This last paragraph is very precise because it says "some of our groups of fighters," which implies that this refers exclusively to soldiers of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, certain groups of our fighters. Whether there is any possibilities of finding others in those groups I don't know, but the telegram is precise. We registered that certain of our fighters from Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, the group of combatants, from a military point of view groups of combatants traveling from Zepa, were they a danger for the Army of Republika Srpska and for the civilian population on the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every group of fighters, and this refers primarily to broken-up groups of fighters, are a threat to every army and the entire population because their behaviour, as a rule, is uncontrolled, undirected, and they are armed and have military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What are the usual actions which an army undertakes when groups of fighters move on the territory over which it has control, a group of enemy fighters, that is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all such situations, first all the organs on the ground are warned, all the commands of the army units. Then the MUP and all the MUP units are warned, and the local authorities are warned who can take action, such as, for example, disseminating information. All the forces on the ground attempt to register such groups and to capture them and disarm them and then hand them over to the competent authorities. Such groups are treated with great caution because one never knows what they will do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now move to a different subject matter. I would like to show the witness Exhibit 5D903. The document in question is an explanation about the authorisation for the passage of convoys and the carrying out of the weekly plan for humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, first of all, could you tell us, what is a notification in the military terminology? And just for the transcript, in your report this is 5D759 on page 35 in the B/C/S version, page 42 in the English version in which you have given us a classification for military documents. Could you please, therefore, explain what is the meaning of the word "notification"?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to repeat the classification made here as regards combat documents. For the most part, they are similar in all armed forces all over the world, and these were valid in the VRS. All combat documents are divided into three groups: first, command; second, information; and the third are auxiliary documents. And from this classification, one can see that information has, for its purpose, obtaining all the elements needed to command, whether something has been done, how it has been done, and whether the command needs to take any corrective action. So this forms into the reporting and information group of documents, the second group.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We know that General Miletic, that some of these notifications entail the name "General Miletic." In paragraph 190 - and this is on page 85 in the English text, page 66 in B/C/S in your report - you stated that General Miletic was involved in the procedure, the decision-making procedure about humanitarian aid and the passage of convoys. Can you tell us what his participation consist in?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reply to your question is in paragraph 191 where I stated that the documents signed by General Miletic are informative documents not having the character of orders. When information had to be sent, when there was no opportunity, as would have been the case in normal conditions, for the Chief of Staff to sign notification documents, then General Miletic signed them and sent them to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So before our eyes what we have is the approval for a weekly plan for humanitarian aid, and this is the approval concerning authorities of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you document 1361, which is a document from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 3rd of April, 1995. Sorry, it's 5D1361.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So as you can see, this is a similar document which also mentions the approval of a weekly plan conducted by UNPROFOR, UNPROFOR movements, except that in this case we are talking about movements within the area of the 2nd Corps and within the boundaries of that area. As a rule, why do armies deliver special authorisations about the convoys of humanitarian organisations and UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every army in Bosnia-Herzegovina was responsible for the situation on its own territory, inter alia security for UNPROFOR units passing through. To ensure security, they delivered these plans for their movements thus pre-empting any surprises.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D783. This is a document from the Drina Corps dated 2nd August, 1993, which conveys to the subordinated units an order from the Main Staff about the passage of UNPROFOR's convoys. The only point I am interested in in this document is on page 2 of the B/C/S version and page 3 in English, and I'm referring to item 13 at the very end. So in B/C/S it's the mention that's at the very bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: According to the order, all misunderstandings with UNPROFOR had to be solved with UNPROFOR including at the meetings which took place with UNPROFOR. Now, in an army when some officers are in charge and attend some meetings, are these officers in charge of a specific area for the agenda of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see here that the original document on cooperation with UNPROFOR was forwarded to the units. One can see that all details had been defined with UNPROFOR, and one can see that the people in the joint commissions were authorised to solve all the problems that had arisen, and if they were not able to do so they would send them up to a higher level where they would be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the Main Staff, would that person be in charge -- would an officer be in charge of UNPROFOR, but an officer who would not attend the meetings with UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then there would be no point. Those working in the commissions, their main task was to attend meetings, to participate in reaching decisions, analyse problems, discuss them with their own command, and then delegate these problems to the meetings that were held.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown 5D1348, please. This is about a meeting with the command of the various armies involved in the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina, a meeting with, also, UNPROFOR. You can see on page 3 in English and in the signed versions that this document was signed by Ratko Mladic for the Republika Srpska representative. Could I now have page 2 in B/C/S, which is also page 2 in the English version. You can see that questions pertaining to the freedom of movement and humanitarian questions were discussed in the course of the meeting. That can be seen under item 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do these questions -- are these questions part of the competencies of the Administration for Operations and Training?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single element of this meeting fell within the purview of the Administration for Operations and Training or, in other words, the competencies of the Administration for Operations and Training cannot be included in any agreement of this type because they're exclusively military competencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: If for one reason or another General Miletic was given competencies about UNPROFOR and humanitarian organisations, would he have had to accompany General Mladic to that meeting, to attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had he been given the authority, then that authority would have been clearly defined, and he would have been duty-bound to attend the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now show you Exhibit 5D1174. This is an order from the president of the republic dated 16th of January, 1994. In item 3 of this order, you can see that all contentious issues or controversial issues in relation with representatives of UNPROFOR must be solved through the corps commands and through the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and that any controversial issue in relation to international humanitarian organisations must be dealt with through the coordinating body of the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Who, according to this order, was in charge of relations with humanitarian organisations, the international humanitarian organisations?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with this order issued by the president of the republic, the problem of military and the problem of humanitarian organisations is clearly defined, and the coordination body of the government is defined in a special document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And who was in charge of the relations with the international humanitarian organisations according to this order?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The coordination body of the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D76 -- 772. It is an order from the Drina Corps dated 10 April, 1993, concerning the control or monitoring of convoys.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the checking of convoys, of humanitarian convoys, was usual -- is usual in wartime?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's absolutely usual. In accordance with what I said previously, the VRS was responsible for the movements of these convoys, for their security, and their coordination. And it was responsible when they were moving through its territory for ensuring that this actually was humanitarian aid and not something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1286? This is an order from the Main Staff. It concerns humanitarian aid. In the first paragraph of this order, one may see that about humanitarian convoys, military equipment was given to the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the carriage or shipping of military milicija, did armies normally allow transporting of military -- of humanitarian -- of military equipment for humanitarian convoys in the other part of the conflict -- to the other part of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No army in the world, including the Army of Republika Srpska, allows humanitarian aid to be transported together with weapons, military equipment, ammunition, and other things that can be used for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see document 5D801. This is an order from the Drina Corps -- a document from the Drina Corps of 25 November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 21st November, 1995, correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document, one sees that -- on the 21st of November, 1993 -- the date is 21 November 1993. In this document, one may see that the Drina Corps and the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska had the information about a possible transfer of explosives and mines in bags which were supposed to be flour bags.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This sort of information, does it normally have an influence on the future passage of the humanitarian convoys and on the checking which may be affected?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information is the result of prior experience, which means that such incidents have been noted and that such acts have been done. And, on the basis of that, all those who manned the check-points were warned, and in that respect I would point out the one-before-last paragraph in B/C/S that -- where it is emphasized that the checks should be made by taking samples and applying methods of inspection that would prevent such things to happen in the future, which means to take all measures to prevent any surprises.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 5D956. This is an information coming from the intelligence department in sector for security and intelligence of the Main Staff, dated 13 August -- I think 1994. In paragraph 2, one may read this: "[In English] We confirmed information that a Turkish UNPROFOR battalion contingent brought in double the combat equipment to the area of Zenica than originally envisaged and gave a specific number of armoured transporters and tanks to the so-called BH Army."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, I am not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [French spoken]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Still the situation is the same. No, I am not blaming anyone. I mean, these things happen. I am just waiting for it to be resolved. No, what I am saying is being transcribed. All right. If you could repeat again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, we haven't --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's solved now. It's solved now. Thank you. Please repeat your question, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It seems that one console is defective in the French booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand this had to be technical because interpretation into B/C/S was being received. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: How is it that this type of information is -- how can it be reflected on the passage of convoys of UNPROFOR and of humanitarian convoys?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This type was information contributed to increased inspections of UNPROFOR and humanitarian aid convoys; for instance, the effect was that the inspection was -- the inspections were more specific about what it is that the units which were moving -- that belonged to the units that were moving through there because up until then, many of those units carried equipment that did not belong to them; secondly, the -- whether the material that was arriving was in fact expended; and third, it pointed to the need for increased inspections of the personnel that were parts of those units.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have Exhibit 5D770. This is an order from the Drina Corps about the movement of UNPROFOR's convoys and about humanitarian convoys, and I'd like to have page 2 both in the B/C/S and in the English versions. And the only point I am interested in here is point number 9, the fact that radio and video equipment is forbidden.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please tell us why video equipment is forbidden?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radio and video equipment are the most sophisticated means or devices used in intelligence. Radio and video equipment allow certain information to be analysed by the best professionals that they had available.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would now like to show to the witness Exhibit 5D842. This is a document from the Main Staff dated 11th of October, 1994, and I would like to have page 2 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Under point 5 of this document, you can see that three people from UNHCR were not able to obtain authorisation to visit Zepa because their intention was to take pictures with a camera. Now, the intention to take pictures or to film or record video, is this something which from a military point of view or for armies is sufficient reason to deny access to a given area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. It is well known that filming is strictly prohibited of certain areas, and combat areas are precisely such sites because they are exposed and they are the focus of the intelligence work of the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D778. This is a document from the Drina Corps from 23rd July, 1993, informing the Main Staff about the fact that radio stations and the satellite antenna was confiscated, taken away from a humanitarian convoy or, rather, a Red Cross convoy, which carried humanitarian aid to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You have already explained what is the meaning of radio equipment. What about the confiscation of this particular equipment which was part of a humanitarian convoy. Is this a usual procedure, again from a military point of view?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely common, and this practice is still in place today. You will see that even delegations that want to visit an area are not allowed to do so, let alone in wartime. So this is something that is just in order to protect one's self from the actions of the other side or from someone acting for the benefit of the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'd like to show you now 5D1271. This is a conversation which is an intercept from 31st August, 1994, which comes from the Croat collection.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this conversation -- I mean, this is a summary of the intercepted conversation between General Brinkman, the head of staff of UNPROFOR, and General Milovanovic. And as you can see, the convoys carrying fuel to the UN units in Srebrenica and Gorazde were not authorised. Can you tell us the meaning of fuel in a conflict?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a conflict fuel, and the meaning of fuel here is primarily military fuel, for military usage, is very important for maneuvers of the other side. Without the fuel, the enemy side will have fewer opportunity for maneuvering and will be able to reach fewer areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would still need another 15 minutes. I'm terribly sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to be sorry, Madam. Incidentally, also fuel in the context of combat operations should never fuel combat operations because the more you fuel it the worse it becomes. We'll stop here for today. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. After 15 minutes I reckon Ms. Fauveau will be finished with her examination, so whoever is next please be prepared. Thank you. General, same advisory as before. Thank you.
